discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body systems with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: J. Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universitat Munich, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Zoller and Cirac showed theoretically that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realize Hubbard-type Hamiltonians with tunable parameters, and proposed controlled atomic systems as quantum simulators of many-body physics. Bloch realized this vision experimentally with the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator transition (2002), then developed quantum gas microscopy, artificial gauge fields and topological bands, and measurements of many-body localization and thermalization. Together they founded a field in which strongly correlated quantum matter is engineered atom by atom, and in which questions about quantum phase transitions, entanglement, non-equilibrium dynamics and open-system physics can be tested with unprecedented precision. Their work transformed atomic physics into a laboratory for condensed-matter and statistical physics, and laid the conceptual and technical foundations of analog quantum simulation, one of the central pillars of today's quantum science and technology.
